metadata.goal: Analyze mobility patterns associated with pick-up and drop-off activities.
metadata.category: Complete daily histories for users with pick-up/drop-off activity, including ordered chain legs, activities, modes, follow-up gaps, destination areas, GPS positions, and point speeds.
metadata.header: MTL Trajet: 21 Pickup Dropoff Daily Chains
metadata.dataset_description: Complete daily histories for users with pick-up/drop-off activity, including ordered chain legs, activities, modes, follow-up gaps, destination areas, GPS positions, and point speeds.
metadata.metric_note: Distances are calculated from delivered GPS polylines; average point speed and duration are synchronized with the point table. Montréal's long island axis runs approximately southwest–northeast, so signed axis displacement summarizes the dominant travel direction.

plot.title: Morning Pick-up/Drop-off and Work Follow-up
plot.description: The plot is generated from the supplied case tables.

insight_list.question: Are morning pick-up/drop-off trips short and motorized, and what follows them?
insight_list.insight: Morning pick-up/drop-off trips are mostly motorized, relatively short, and often followed by longer work trips departing soon from the same area.

plot.title: Afternoon Pick-up/Drop-off Chain Position
plot.description: The plot is generated from the supplied case tables.

insight_list.question: Where do afternoon pick-up/drop-off trips occur in daily chains and what follows them?
insight_list.insight: Afternoon pick-up/drop-off trips occur later in daily chains and are more often followed by return-home trips than additional work travel.

plot.title: Repeated PUDO Windows and Daily Variation
plot.description: The plot is generated from the supplied case tables.

insight_list.question: Do repeated users retain similar pick-up/drop-off windows and areas while the rest of their day varies?
insight_list.insight: Users with repeated pick-up/drop-off days keep similar departure windows and destination areas, while their remaining daily routes vary.

plot.title: Active-mode Pick-up/Drop-off Exceptions
plot.description: The plot is generated from the supplied case tables.

insight_list.question: Which pick-up/drop-off trips use active modes without an immediate motorized follow-up?
insight_list.insight: A few pick-up/drop-off trips use walking or cycling within mixed-use areas and are not followed by an immediate motorized trip.

insights: Morning pick-up/drop-off trips are mostly motorized, relatively short, and often followed by longer work trips departing soon from the same area.
Afternoon pick-up/drop-off trips occur later in daily chains and are more often followed by return-home trips than additional work travel.
Users with repeated pick-up/drop-off days keep similar departure windows and destination areas, while their remaining daily routes vary.
A few pick-up/drop-off trips use walking or cycling within mixed-use areas and are not followed by an immediate motorized trip.
summary: Morning pick-up/drop-off is short and predominantly motorized; most, but not all, are promptly followed from the same area by longer work travel. Afternoon pick-up/drop-off occurs later and usually precedes home; repeat users retain stable PUDO windows and areas despite variation elsewhere in the day, with six delayed active-mode exceptions.
evidence_policy: Claims describe patterns in this controlled constructed dataset and do not establish causal relationships.
